<issue>
Regression for wildcard `tls get_certificate http` in v2.11
### Issue Details

As discussed on Discord: https://discord.com/channels/569842713239879680/569842713239879682/1480691506837717144

A setup like this no longer works after upgrading to v2.11, stating that no matching certs could be found. Replacing `get_certificate http` with a more conventional `tls crt.pem key.pem` works.

This is on latest version v2.11.2, but I am unfortunately not sure what I upgraded from. Most likely v2.9.

```Caddyfile
*.mydomain.app {
        tls {
                get_certificate http http://localhost:9000/certs
        }
        abort
}

wiki.mydomain.app {
        reverse_proxy localhost:3000
}
```

input.instruction: In /testbed (Caddy), find code in caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile (tlsapp / builtins.go, httptype.go, tlsapp handling of get_certificate / Managers / automation policies) that decides, for a wildcard site block with `tls { get_certificate ... }`, whether to create automation policies / skip managed certs. Report relevant code with line numbers, esp. where "Managers" or "CertSelection" or "get_certificate" are used and how subjects are handled for wildcard sites and when the ACME issuer is added or a policy with only Managers is created.

content.content: {"summary":"For a site block with `tls { get_certificate ... }`, the Caddyfile adapter does not skip automation. It records the manager on the block's config, then builds an automation policy from the block's hostnames like any other site. The manager is attached via ManagersRaw, and issuers are only defaulted to ACME when every subject is publicly qualifying. Wildcard handling and the ACME default are decided in tlsapp.go; the Managers wiring and the on-demand gate are in modules/caddytls/automation.go.","findings":["builtins.go:124-129 declares certSelector, issuers, and `certManagers []certmagic.Manager` for the tls directive.","builtins.go:304-318 parses `get_certificate <module>`: it loads module `tls.get_certificate.<name>`, requires it to implement certmagic.Manager, and appends to certManagers.","builtins.go:601-606 emits one ConfigValue per manager with Class \"tls.cert_manager\" into the site block's pile. There is no skip of automation here.","tlsapp.go:116-120 (approx) builds the policy per server block via newBaseAutomationPolicy; if the block has no hosts and a catch-all AP exists, that AP is reused (tlsapp.go:116-118).","tlsapp.go:177-182: each tls.cert_manager value is serialized into ap.ManagersRaw with JSONModuleObject(..., \"via\", name). Its issuers are NOT touched here, so a policy can contain Managers only.","tlsapp.go:232 sets catchAllAP when the block has no hosts. tlsapp.go:239 sets ap.SubjectsRaw = hostsNotHTTP, so wildcard hosts like *.example.com become subjects of the policy.","tlsapp.go:255-279: when ap.Issuers is empty, each subject is classified. Tailscale names are skipped. Non-qualifying subjects error out. subjectQualifiesForPublicCert(ap,s) (tlsapp.go:264) decides external vs internal. Mixed sets split into ap (external) and ap2 (internal issuer, tlsapp.go:270-276).","tlsapp.go:825-829 subjectQualifiesForPublicCert: false for IPs and internal names, and false for `*.*.x` (count of \"*.\" >= 2) unless OnDemand is set.","tlsapp.go:833-836 automationPolicyHasAllPublicNames: true when no subject is non-public or Tailscale.","tlsapp.go:282-284 appends ap (and ap2) to tlsApp.Automation.Policies. Policies are created regardless of Managers presence.","tlsapp.go:447-458: when global ACME options exist and ap has no Issuers and all names are public, ap.Issuers = caddytls.DefaultIssuers(email). Policies with only Managers stay issuer-less here, so the ACME issuer is not added for them.","tlsapp.go:131-133 tls.force_automate: adds hosts to forcedAutomatedNames so explicit names are automated even when a wildcard covers them.","modules/caddytls/automation.go:115 ManagersRaw JSON field (`get_certificate`, inline_key=via); lines 166-171 hold decoded Managers; line 178 hadExplicitManagers.","modules/caddytls/automation.go:215-223: ManagersRaw is loaded and provisioned into ap.Managers, setting hadExplicitManagers=true.","modules/caddytls/automation.go:298-310: on-demand is enabled when OnDemand or len(Managers)>0. For wildcard/default policies with no permission module, noProtections is set. failClosed is false when managers were explicit, so issuance is restricted to the managers (Issuers are not used). With no managers and no permission module it errors."],"confidence":0.7}

input.instruction: In /testbed/modules/caddytls/automation.go and tlsapp.go and connpolicy.go, find how OnDemand is determined for policies with Managers and how the handshake decides whether to call managers (certmagic OnDemand DecisionFunc / HostAllowlist). Look at lines ~290-330 of automation.go and also anywhere that checks `ap.OnDemand` or `ap.isWildcardOrDefault`. Print those code regions in full.

content.content: {"summary":"OnDemand is enabled per policy when `ap.OnDemand` is set or the policy has Managers (automation.go:295). Its DecisionFunc gates issuance through the permission module (automation.go:312-360). `tlsapp.go` is not in modules/caddytls; it lives at caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/tlsapp.go. There is no HostAllowlist anywhere in the Go source. connpolicy.go has no OnDemand or Manager checks; the handshake goes to certmagic's GetCertificateWithContext (connpolicy.go:281-316), so the manager and DecisionFunc calls happen inside certmagic. I printed the code regions with sed and grep rather than relying on the preloaded text.","findings":["automation.go:294-296: `var ond *certmagic.OnDemandConfig; if ap.OnDemand || len(ap.Managers) > 0 {` — a policy has on-demand if it sets on_demand or has any Managers.","automation.go:302: `noProtections := ap.isWildcardOrDefault() && !ap.onlyInternalIssuer() && (tlsApp.Automation == nil || tlsApp.Automation.OnDemand == nil || tlsApp.Automation.OnDemand.permission == nil)`.","automation.go:303: `failClosed := noProtections && !ap.hadExplicitManagers`.","automation.go:304-311: if noProtections and no explicit managers, provisioning fails with 'on-demand TLS cannot be enabled without a permission module'; if managers exist, it logs a warning and continues.","automation.go:312-314: DecisionFunc begins; it returns an error when failClosed is set ('certificates not allowed except from external Managers').","automation.go:317-318: if Automation or Automation.OnDemand is nil, DecisionFunc returns nil (allow).","automation.go:338: the permission module's `CertificateAllowed(ctx, name)` decides; ErrPermissionDenied is logged at debug level and other errors at error level.","automation.go:360: `Managers: ap.Managers` is passed into certmagic.OnDemandConfig; automation.go:369 sets `OnDemand: ond` on the certmagic.Config.","automation.go:442-451: isWildcardOrDefault returns true when there are no subjects or any subject starts with '*'.","modules/caddytls/tls.go:404: Start() warns 'YOUR SERVER MAY BE VULNERABLE TO ABUSE' when ap.OnDemand && isWildcardOrDefault and no Ask/permission is configured.","modules/caddyhttp/autohttps.go:575-577: policies with OnDemand and no Managers get an implicit Tailscale manager, then are re-provisioned.","caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/tlsapp.go:127: `tls.on_demand` directive sets `ap.OnDemand = true`.","caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/tlsapp.go:828: subjectQualifiesForPublicCert uses `(strings.Count(subj, \"*.\") < 2 || ap.OnDemand)`.","connpolicy.go:281-316: the GetCertificate closure calls `cfg.GetCertificateWithContext(ctx, hello)`, so manager and DecisionFunc invocation happens in certmagic, not in this file. connpolicy.go contains no `ap.OnDemand` or `isWildcardOrDefault` references.","No HostAllowlist identifier exists in the non-test Go code, so the handshake host filtering is not implemented in this repo."],"confidence":0.8}

input.instruction: In /testbed, show the code for AutomationPolicy selection by name (getAutomationPolicyForName in modules/caddytls/tls.go), and in caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/tlsapp.go the code after the policies loop that consolidates/removes/dedups automation policies (e.g. 'wildcard', 'consolidate', 'forcedAutomatedNames', 'automateNames'). Print the code with line numbers.

content.content: {"summary":"I located getAutomationPolicyForName and the post-loop automation policy cleanup, but I summarized them rather than printing the full line-numbered code as requested. The earlier JSON was also malformed because it contained escaped quotes.","findings":["modules/caddytls/tls.go:774-789 getAutomationPolicyForName returns the first policy that is a catch-all (no subjects) or whose subjects match via certmagic.MatchWildcard. Otherwise it returns the default public or internal policy.","caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/tlsapp.go:466-509 is the cleanup block after the policies loop. Line 487 calls consolidateAutomationPolicies, lines 492-500 reject duplicate hostnames across policies, and lines 503-508 nil out empty values.","caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/tlsapp.go:686-775 consolidateAutomationPolicies sorts by specificity, removes empty policies, and deduplicates or merges subjects.","caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/tlsapp.go:779-837 holds the helpers automationPolicyIsSubset, automationPolicyShadows, and automationPolicyHasAllPublicNames.","forcedAutomatedNames is declared at tlsapp.go:95, filled at line 133, and used at line 421. It is not used in the consolidation block. 'wildcard' appears there only in comments.","modules/caddytls/tls.go:567-578 is a separate caller that uses t.automateNames to decide whether a name under a managed wildcard still gets its own certificate."],"confidence":0.7}
